summary: Configured node1 to record sudo commands with timestamps and users in `/var/log/sudo-commands.log`, without duplicating them into general system logs. Configuration and logging remained healthy after reboot.
actions_performed: Added `/etc/sudoers.d/command-logging` with a dedicated logfile, four-digit years, and sudo syslog output disabled.
Verified uniquely marked sudo commands were recorded with timestamp, invoking user, target user, working directory, and command.
Verified those markers were absent from `/var/log/messages` and `/var/log/secure`.
Rebooted node1 safely and confirmed its boot identity changed from `32e1f4e0-0ae4-4b67-9b90-4ddc6c4ce51e` to `5c49e9ee-8e6d-44b8-96bf-f28076f49b33`.
Confirmed the configuration, previous log data, rsyslog health, and new sudo logging all survived the reboot.

evidence.requirement: Record sudo commands with user and timestamp in `/var/log/sudo-commands.log`
evidence.summary: The configuration parsed successfully, and the dedicated log captured the test command with year-bearing timestamp, invoking user `root`, target user, working directory, and command.

evidence.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of the general system log
evidence.summary: Before and after reboot, unique sudo-command markers were absent from both `/var/log/messages` and `/var/log/secure`.

Evidence captures the healthy baseline, accepted reboot schedule, temporary disconnection, changed boot ID, active/enabled rsyslog, valid persistent sudoers configuration, preserved pre-reboot record, and successful post-reboot command logging.
